question: Will the UK increase the qualifying period for settlement to 10 years before May 2026?
summary: Official materials show strong policy momentum toward a 10-year earned settlement baseline.
Public consultation and proposed reductions for contributions support adoption, but do not guarantee timing.
Legislative and operational rollout risks could delay changes beyond May 2026.
Transitional arrangements and potential legal challenges add further near-term timing uncertainty.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections are valid and highlight timing and rollout risks; they indicate possible delays but do not overturn the direction toward a 10-year baseline.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted downward from 0.93 to 0.86 to account for delivery risks (parliamentary approval, transitional arrangements, and rollout complexities) while preserving the underlying trend toward a 10-year earned settlement.

forecasts.reference-class: UK immigration settlement policy reform proposals (earned settlement) to raise the baseline qualifying period from five to ten years, with a close public consultation in 2025–2026 and potential implementation in 2026.

sources.claim: The Home Secretary announced a proposed new contribution-based settlement model requiring a minimum of 10 years' lawful residence before settlement, effectively doubling the current period, with the plans to be subject to a consultation.
The Earned Settlement consultation sets out a default 10-year qualifying period for settlement, with further options and conditions to earn reductions based on contribution and other criteria.
Freeths reports that the baseline qualifying period will increase to at least 10 years under the proposed earned settlement, with the consultation open until February 12, 2026.
Moore SGD Law notes the 12-week consultation closing date of February 12, 2026 and suggests changes could take effect as soon as April 2026.

Guardian reporting indicates the immigration white paper proposed moving from automatic settlement after five years to a 10-year (or longer) earned settlement framework, affecting around 1.5 million workers.
The immigration white paper Restoring control over the immigration system (May 12, 2025) outlines reforms including raising the standard settlement qualifying period to 10 years.
Earned settlement consultation states baseline qualifying period will be increased from 5 to 10 years, with reductions for contributions.
Nov 20, 2025 government announces the 10-year baseline with reductions as part of a major overhaul of the legal migration model.
House of Commons Library briefing summarises the 2025 immigration white paper proposals, including a 10-year baseline with exemptions, announced 20 November 2025.
Prime Minister announces plan to extend settlement path to 10 years as part of Plan for Change.
Media reports that the white paper would extend the wait for permanent settlement to 10 years, with potential retroactivity.
Guardian opinion piece arguing that extending to 10 years is unfair and may be challenged.

Government consultation on earned settlement proposes increasing the baseline qualifying period for settlement to 10 years, with possible reductions or increases based on contribution, integration, and other criteria.

Parliamentary briefing notes that the May 2025 Immigration White Paper proposed raising the standard qualifying period from five to ten years, with a timetable suggesting changes could begin in April 2026 and final decisions after consultation.
Long residence guidance confirms a 10-year continuous lawful presence baseline for settlement via the long-residence route.
Industry commentary notes the Home Office consultation on Earned Settlement aims to raise the standard qualifying period to 10 years, with a closing date around February 12, 2026.
